basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 7.' and it opens 'Vers. 7. Decem vicibus mutavit mercedem. Subauditur, meam. Cum enim videret Laban varios'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 7. Decem vicibus mutavit mercedem. Subauditur, meam. Cum enim videret Laban varios fetus augeri, mutata conditione dicebat: Volo ut varii fetus meae partis sint, pecus vero unius coloris tuae sit partis. Rursus cum videret et nigra multiplicari, mutata rursus conditione haec sibi assumebat. Tali modo decem vicibus dicit eum Jacob suam mutasse | mercedem. Typice Laban, qui interpretatur dealbatio, diabolum significat, qui licet sit suo merito tenebrosus, tamen transfigurat se in angelum lucis.
